Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the MedTech Innovations Inc. Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. To ask a question, you may press star then one on your telephone. Please note, this call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Thompson, VP of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson:
Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today. Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that this call will contain forward-looking statements, including expectations regarding our future performance, business outlook, and financial results. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Joining me on today's call are Mark Reynolds, CEO; David Chen, CFO; Dr. Elena Vasquez, Chief Technology Officer; and Raj Patel, Chief Commercial Officer.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Mark Reynolds.

Mark Reynolds:
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. MedTech Innovations Inc. delivered strong results this quarter, driven by increasing adoption of our innovative medical devices and strategic partnerships.

Today, I will cover five key aspects of our performance:
1. R&D investment and innovation pipeline progress
2. Organic revenue growth by segment and geography
3. Impact of pricing and cost management initiatives
4. New product launches and contribution to growth
5. Revenue and margin guidance for the next quarter/year

David will then provide a more detailed review of our financials. After that, we'll open the call for your questions.

Now, let's get started with R&D investment and innovation pipeline progress.

Our R&D efforts remain a cornerstone of our long-term growth strategy in the medical devices sector, where staying ahead in areas like value-based care, minimally invasive procedures, and AI-integrated digital therapeutics is essential for gaining market share against competitors such as Medtronic, Boston Scientific, and Abbott. We're leading in promising high-margin areas including structural heart, neuromodulation, and robotics.

In the first half of fiscal 2024, we allocated $458 million to R&D, which equated to 14.2% of net revenue—an increase from 13.1% in the same period last year and a 12% rise in absolute terms. This supports our full-year target of $950 million to $1.0 billion in R&D spending, despite challenges like higher costs for clinical trials and attracting top talent amid inflation. This level positions us at the high end compared to industry peers averaging 11-13% of revenue, and we anticipate these investments will generate over $1.2 billion in additional revenue by 2027 through new product introductions.

By therapeutic focus, cardiovascular took 42% of our spending at $192 million year-to-date, capitalizing on structural heart procedure growth with global TAVR volumes up 15% year-over-year according to iData Research. Orthopedics and spine received 28% or $128 million, eyeing the $60 billion market driven by aging populations. Neuromodulation and robotics combined for 22% or $101 million, riding the robotics sector's expected 18% compound annual growth rate to 2030 as forecasted by Grand View Research. The remaining 8% went to digital health and AI platforms, up from 5% last year, as we incorporate predictive analytics into our device ecosystems.

Pipeline-wise, we achieved six major milestones across 24 programs this quarter, with eight products reaching late-stage development, ready for Phase III equivalents or IDE and PMA submissions. In cardiovascular, our VitaFlow Neo drug-eluting bioresorbable scaffold completed enrollment in its pivotal IDE trial involving 1,200 patients at 45 U.S. and European sites, showing a 95% device success rate and just 2.1% 30-day major adverse cardiac events, surpassing the Absorb BRS that encountered recalls. We expect FDA IDE approval in Q4 2024 and CE Mark under MDR in the first half of 2025, targeting the $4.5 billion coronary intervention opportunity. Our AI-enhanced drug-coated balloon for below-the-knee peripheral artery disease earned FDA breakthrough status, with Phase II data indicating 88% primary patency at 12 months—15 percentage points better than Lutonix or IN.PACT.

In structural heart, the TricValve Neo transcatheter tricuspid repair system finished its U.S. pivotal trial early, with 450 high-risk patients achieving 85% procedural success and 72% reduction from severe to mild tricuspid regurgitation at one year. This fills a gap in the $2 billion tricuspid space, where Edwards Lifesciences' Cardioband is still expanding. We've filed PMA module 1 with the FDA and project mid-2025 approval, with $150 million in first-year U.S. launch sales.

For orthopedics, the AugmentX 3D-printed trabecular titanium spinal implant earned CE Mark under the stringent MDR—passed on first review by only 30% of applicants—and we're pursuing U.S. 510(k) clearance after preclinical tests exceeding 5 million fatigue cycles, 20% beyond Stryker's Tritanium. EU orders surged 25% year-over-year in Q2 in Germany and France thanks to HTA reimbursements, and we're teaming with a leading Japanese distributor for a Q1 2025 APAC debut in the $1.2 billion spine market growing at 9% annually.

Neuromodulation highlights include the PrecisionPulse closed-loop spinal cord stimulation system, using AI for adaptive therapy, which posted Phase III interim results of 67% pain relief in chronic back pain cases versus 52% for Medtronic's Intellis. FDA filing is set for Q3 2024, while EU early access has yielded $12 million. In robotics, our EndoFlex platform for flexible endoscopy, paired with AI navigation, completed first-in-human procedures in Asia via an investigator trial, achieving 96% completion in tough GI cases. We're committing $75 million to challenge Intuitive Surgical's da Vinci and Stryker's Mako, emphasizing single-use tools for recurring revenue.

We've optimized our portfolio by divesting two early programs to focus on high-return items aiming for over 20% gross margins on launches. Key partnerships, like Google Cloud for AI training—which sped development by 30%—and our $200 million venture fund backing five digital twin startups for device simulations to ease FDA virtual trial reviews, are accelerating progress.

On regulations, we've secured three U.S. IDE approvals year-to-date, while buffering EU MDR delays averaging 18 months now versus 12 before 2021 through paths in Australia and Japan. In China and India, where medtech imports rose 22% per IQVIA, we're localizing production for NMPA compliance under Made in China 2025, unlocking $300 million in value. Our R&D returns stand at 3.8 times for 2020-2022 investments, thanks to successes like CardioGuard ICD, fueling mid-teens organic growth versus the sector's 6-8%.

Now, let's talk about organic revenue growth by segment and geography.

Our Q2 organic revenue expanded 9.2% year-over-year on a constant-currency basis—the best in three years and above our guidance—demonstrating core strength despite inflation on materials like biocompatible polymers and nitinol, plus supply issues for precision parts from Southeast Asia. Stripping out a 2.1% FX drag, mainly from a firm USD versus euro and yen, reported revenue rose 7.1% to $2.85 billion. This stemmed from higher procedure volumes, 1-2% average selling price gains from our premium transcatheter and robotic tech, and new product revenue at 28% of segment sales, up from 24%.

By segment: Cardiovascular, 46% of revenue at $1.31 billion, grew 12.4% organically, powered by structural heart at 18.7% via VitalFlow Ultra—a low-profile, repositionable TAVR valve with superior annular sealing to Edwards' Sapien 3 Ultra—gaining 2.2 U.S. share points to 31%. Global procedures climbed 15%, aided by low-risk expansions and AI imaging. Cardiac rhythm management rose 8.2%, with ICDs and leadless pacemakers like VitalPulse Nano at 35% new product share, countering ablation softness from Biosense Webster competition.

Orthopedics and spine, 22% or $627 million, advanced 7.9%, as elective backlogs cleared post-Omicron. Hip/knee recon hit 9.5% led by cementless Trinity stems and Corin robotics, up 22% in U.S. ASCs mirroring outpatient shifts. Spine instrumentation gained 6.1% on expandable interbodies for minimally invasive fusions, though flat ASPs from GPO bundles; we're countering via value-based partnerships like Zimmer Biomet's ROSA.

Endoscopy and MedSurg, 18% at $513 million, grew 6.3%, with single-use PureView duodenoscopes up 25% post-FDA expansions tackling CRE risks, akin to Olympus scopes. MedSurg consumables rose 5.8% on antimicrobial catheters for HAI prevention.

Diabetes and neuromodulation, 9% or $256 million, increased 4.7%, diabetes at 6.2% via VitalSense implantable CGM matching Dexcom G7 accuracy with 14-day wear at 40% new product. Neuromodulation softened to 2.1% on EU VNS reimbursement issues, but DBS refresh with adaptive algorithms eyes H2 lift like Medtronic Percept PC.

Other categories like diagnostics and emerging tech, 5% at $142 million, surged 11.2% on rapid troponin assays up 16% with ER rebounds.

Geographically, U.S. at 65% led with 11.8% organic growth from CMS TAVR/robotic payments, ASC ortho at 28%, and 1.5 share points gained over Stryker/Abbott. EMEA at 18% grew 5.4% despite MDR delays like Boston Scientific's Watchman, offset by 12% German CGM coverage; UK/France up 7-9% on demographics. APAC 12% at 8.9%, China 14.2% post-COVID on VitalFlow tenders in 45 hospitals, Japan 6.5% robotics despite ASP pressure, India/ASEAN 10% via direct strategies. LATAM/Canada 5% at 3.2%, up sequentially on Mexico CRM wins.

Key drivers: procedure upticks at 7-9% globally per IQVIA, innovation with 15 FDA 510(k)s/8 CE Marks like peripheral bioresorbables for $2.5 billion TAM, and ops excellence with 150 basis points gross margin to 68.5% via Mexico/Ireland localization against 10-15% resin hikes. We're prioritizing TAVR (15% CAGR), robotics (20%), CGMs (25%), navigating GPO/GLP-1 headwinds with $1.2 billion R&D (12% sales) for 20+ launches by FY2026 like CAR-T delivery. Q3 eyes 8-10%, full-year 9% versus consensus 5-7%.

Moving on to the impact of pricing and cost management initiatives.

These efforts fueled over 300 basis points gross margin expansion to 68.2%, topping guidance and peers like Abbott/Boston Scientific at 65-66% amid reimbursement and supply strains. In MedTech, where margins average mid-60s, this discipline is vital.

Pricing first: Facing CMS bundles capping TAVR/joint ASPs at 3-4%, we used GPO renewals, value-based models, portfolio tweaks. U.S. (52% revenue) got mid-single-digit hikes on 75% cardiovascular like CoreValve TAVR/Hugo RAS, Vizient/Premier deals at 2.8% average offsetting 1.2% sequestration, adding $285 million and 150bps to realization. Europe shifted neuromodulation like Percept PC to outcomes-based at €28,500/unit versus 5% drop prior, covering 40% MedSurg for €120 million preserved. Emerging APAC/LATAM (18%) premium-priced EverPulse ICDs 12-15% above MicroPort in China (22% defib share), Triathlon knees at INR 450,000 vs. generics in India (25% growth). Net: 2.1% swing, 90bps margin boost offsetting 1.5% FX.

Costs via 'MedTech Efficiency 2.0' target $1.2 billion savings by FY2025, $450 million year-to-date. Supply chain: cut top 50 suppliers 20%, shifted 35% non-implants to Vietnam/Mexico for 14% structural heart COGS drop ($180 million), AI forecasting via SAP IBP trimmed inventory 22% to $2.1 billion at 98.7% service. Manufacturing: Six Sigma cut ortho defects 18%, cobots in Ireland up Micra throughput 25% ($1,200 to $950/unit), site shifts saved 9% labor with 45X credits. R&D: design-for-manufacturability like 3D titanium rods cut intro costs 15%, time-to-market 20% to 24 months; SG&A down 7% to 24.1% via attrition. Total 210bps: supply 120, manufacturing 60, overhead 30. Ortho to 71%, cardio 69%, diabetes 72%—beating estimates.

Embedded amid consolidation like J&J-Abiomed, countering ortho biosimilars/GLP-1. U.S. IRA bundles negotiated insulin pumps 3-year floors; EU MDR front-loaded $250 million but sped approvals 10%. Ahead: 1.5-2% pricing, $600 million cost run-rate, margins trough 68.5% Q4 to 70%+ FY2025, 12-14% EPS growth; hedging steel tariffs, eyeing China upside.

Next, new product launches and contribution to growth.

New products drove $285 million in Q2, 28% of device sales, fueling 22% organic segment growth—beating Evaluate MedTech's mid-single digits. Over 18 months, three launches targeted adjacencies in aging demographics, value care, efficiency.

CardioFlex Pro DCB for PAD got FDA PMA Q4 2023 post-IDE with 85% 12-month patency vs. Medtronic IN.PACT's 72%; Q2 U.S. $120 million, +65% sequential, 72% margins on paclitaxel polymer cutting revascularization 40%. $7.5 billion PAD CAGR to 2030 on diabetes surge; EU CE Mark 15% Germany/UK share on DRGs.

NeuroStim Elite SCS launched Q1 2024, rechargeable MRI-conditional with AI adaptive stim ahead of Boston Scientific WaveWriter; 500-patient registry 55% opioid drop at six months for CMS non-drug push. Q2 $95 million, 35% neuromod segment +45% YoY; China NMPA/Fosun 120% APAC QoQ on 12% CAGR.

OrthoGuide AI robotic navigation 510(k)-cleared post-AAOS soft launch; cuts fluoro 60%, screws <2% vs. da Vinci ortho; Q2 $70 million bookings, 18% ortho growth, 68% margins on $5,000/case AI subs. Vizient/Premier GPOs 25% attach to OrthoFlex.

Total 450bps top-line add, 32% adoption top 500 U.S. accounts vs. Leerink norm; $180 million Q2 R&D (12%) on bioresorbables/closed-loop, 15 IDE/PMA incl. low-risk TAVR vs. Sapien 3 Ultra. U.S. 55%, Europe 25% Horizon funding, EM 20% vs. Chinese imports. TAM to $65 billion by 2027 via hybrid suites, data monetization, $450 million BioPulse M&A for VNS. FY2024 NPR $1.2 billion, 30%+ growth 500bps margins; pipeline like coronary scaffold.

Finally, revenue and margin guidance for the next quarter/year.

Q2 hit $2.85 billion revenue up 9.2% organic, 68.2% gross margins. Q3: $2.65-$2.75 billion, 6-10% organic incl. 2% M&A like NeuroStim DBS tuck-in akin Medtronic Percept. Cardio $1.38-$1.43 billion 8-12% on EvoFlow TAVR 25% attach, EP mid-teens FlexSense vs. SmartTouch; ortho $740-$770 million 5-9% Mako knees 20% QoQ; neuro/other $530-$550 million flat-+4% AI SCS ramp. U.S. 8-11% Medicare OPPS $22,000 TAVR; EMEA 4-7% NICE/French AFib; APAC 10-14% China FlexSense 50 accounts/Japan demo. Gross 66-67% +50bps midpoint mix/disposables 68%; op 24.5-25.5%, OpEx 41-42% $120 million R&D Siemens AI; EPS $1.52-$1.58 2.1 billion shares 22% tax.

FY2024 raised: $10.65-$10.85 billion 7-9% organic vs. prior $10.4-$10.7 billion, 1% FX. Cardio mid-teens TAVR+25%/EP+18%; ortho 6-8% robotics 30% knees; neuro 5-7%. Gross 66.5-67.5% +150bps $250 million savings/resin ease; op 25-26%, R&D 12.5% $500 million robotic PCI vs. Polaris; EPS $6.45-$6.65 +9-12%. Pillars: procedures +5% pre-COVID per Definitive, AI like EvoFlow leak cut 30%; $1.2 billion buybacks $800 million M&A wearables. Risks: policy, talc $150 million, China; $4.2 billion cash 1.8x leverage.

I will now turn the call over to David for a review of our financial results.

David Chen:
Thank you, Mark. As Mark highlighted, we achieved robust financial outcomes this quarter, with revenue of $2.85 billion up 7.1% reported and 9.2% organic. Gross margins expanded 300 basis points to 68.2%, driven by the pricing and cost initiatives Mark detailed, plus favorable product mix. Operating expenses rose modestly in line with R&D acceleration to 14.2% of revenue, while SG&A benefited from efficiency gains. Adjusted operating margin hit 25.2%, and diluted EPS came in at $1.62, exceeding expectations. Cash flow from operations was strong at $650 million, supporting $300 million in share repurchases and pipeline investments. Balance sheet remains solid with $4.2 billion liquidity. These results validate our strategy and underpin the raised full-year outlook Mark shared. Margins reflect supply chain shifts and manufacturing gains, positioning us for continued leverage.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Dr. Vasquez for an update on our product pipeline.

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, David. Our innovation pipeline continues to advance rapidly, building on the R&D momentum Mark outlined. We recently received FDA clearance for VitaFlow Neo, our next-generation bioresorbable scaffold that enhances coronary interventions with superior safety and efficacy profiles. This device promises to transform patient outcomes in structural heart by reducing long-term complications and enabling vessel restoration. Beyond that, TricValve Neo and PrecisionPulse are on track for key approvals, with early data exceeding benchmarks. EndoFlex robotics first-in-human success opens doors in GI, and AugmentX spine implants are gaining EU traction. Our AI integrations across platforms are accelerating development cycles and improving precision, with partnerships enhancing scalability. This pipeline supports sustained growth in high-margin areas.

Now, back to Mark for Q&A.

Mark Reynolds:
Thank you, Elena. Operator, we are now ready to take questions.

Operator:
Thank you. Instructions for asking questions: press star then one. Our first question comes from Alex Rivera with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Thanks, and congrats on the quarter. Mark, on the R&D pipeline, can you elaborate on ROI expectations for neuromodulation and robotics, especially with the divestitures and partnerships?

Mark Reynolds:
Great question, Alex. Our neuromodulation investments, like PrecisionPulse, are tracking to 3.8x returns similar to past cohorts, with Phase III data showing strong pain relief advantages. Robotics via EndoFlex targets recurring revenue from single-use, with $75 million committed to match Intuitive and Stryker scale. Divestitures sharpened focus on 20%+ margin launches, while Google Cloud cut timelines 30%, and ventures de-risk FDA paths. Overall, these fuel mid-teens growth.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Jamie Lee with J.P. Morgan. Please go ahead.

Jamie Lee:
Thanks. David, with organic growth at 9.2%, how sustainable is the U.S. 11.8% and APAC rebound, particularly China tenders and EMEA MDR?

David Chen:
Jamie, U.S. leverage from CMS payments and ASC shift is durable, with 1.5 share points gained. China post-COVID at 14.2% via VitalFlow in 45 hospitals sets H2 strength; APAC 8.9% overall. EMEA 5.4% navigates delays like Watchman but gains CGM coverage. Q3 8-10% holds on seasonality, full-year 9%.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Taylor Kim with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Taylor Kim:
Hi, team. Raj, on commercial execution, how are pricing initiatives landing with GPOs and payers, and impact on ortho/spine adoption?

Raj Patel:
Thanks, Taylor. Pricing secured 2.8% U.S. uplifts via Vizient/Premier on high-volume cardio/ortho, preserving $285 million. Value-based bundles stabilized EU ASPs, EM premiums beat locals. OrthoGuide robotics at 25% attach drives spine uptake despite GPO bundles, ASCs key for Trinity stems. Adoption accelerating to 32% in top accounts.

Mark Reynolds:
Thank you for that insight, Raj.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Chris Patel with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Chris Patel:
Congrats. Elena, details on AI/digital health pipeline integration, timelines for DCB and tricuspid, and competitive moats?

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Chris, AI optimizes DCB for PAD with 88% patency, breakthrough status on track Q4 IDE. TricValve Neo PMA module filed, mid-2025 U.S. with 72% TR reduction. Moats via adaptive algorithms in SCS/DBS outperforming Intellis/Percept, cloud data for OR efficiency. Digital at 8% spend up, predictive analytics embedded ecosystem-wide.

Mark Reynolds:
Thank you for your questions. Before we conclude, I want to thank our employees, customers, and partners for their continued support. We are confident in our ability to continue delivering strong results and creating value for our shareholders.

Thank you for joining us today.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
